States men's national under-19 basketball team|Team]]}} }} '''Samuel Thomas Dekker''' (born May 6, 1994) is an American [[college basketball]] coach and former professional player who currently serves as an assistant men’s basketball coach for the [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina Gamecocks]] of the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC). Dekker played [[college basketball]] for the [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin Badgers]]. After finishing college on a [[2015 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|championship game run in the 2015 NCAA Tournament]], Dekker was selected by the [[Houston Rockets]] with the 18th overall pick in the [[2015 NBA draft]].{{cite news|first=Katie|last=DeLong|title=NBA Draft: Houston Rockets select former Badgers forward Sam Dekker at #21|url=http://fox6now.com/2015/06/25/nba-draft-houston-rockets-select-former-badgers-forward-sam-dekker-at-21|publisher=WITI-FOX6|date=June 25, 2015|access-date=June 26, 2015}} ==High school career== Dekker was named the Wisconsin Gatorade Player of the Year following his senior season. He was also named 2012 [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]], [[Associated Press|AP]] first-team all-state and [[Wisconsin Mr. Basketball|Wisconsin Basketball Coaches' Association's Mr. Basketball]] award. He led [[Sheboygan Lutheran High School|Sheboygan Lutheran]] to the school's first-ever [[Wisconsin Interscholastic Athletic Association|WIAA]] state title. Dekker scored 40 points, including the last 12, in the state title game including the game-winning three-point shot with two seconds left.{{cite web|title=Sam Dekker Wisconsin Badgers profile|url=http://www.uwbadgers.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/sam_dekker_801183.html|publisher=UWBadgers.com|access-date=March 28, 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131209193016/http://www.uwbadgers.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/sam_dekker_801183.html|archive-date=December 9, 2013}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|collapse=no|year=2012}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Sam Dekker | position = SF | hometown = Sheboygan, WI | highschool = Sheboygan Lutheran | feet = 6 | inches = 7 | weight = 195 | 40 = | commitdate = 6/15/2010 | scout stars = 5 | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | grayshirt = }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2012 | rivals ref title = 2012 Wisconsin Commitments | scout ref title = Men's Basketball Recruiting | espn ref title = ESPN- Wisconsin Badgers Men's Basketball Recruiting | espn schoolid = | scout overall = 4 ([[Small forward|SF]]) | rivals overall = 3 (SF) | espn overall = 4 (SF) | accessdate = December 10, 2011 | bball = yes }} ==College career== [[File:Sam Dekker 2012.jpg|thumb|Dekker with Wisconsin in 2012]] ===Freshman season=== Dekker played in 35 games (3 starts) as a freshman on the [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin Badgers]]. He was one of only four true freshman to start under [[Bo Ryan]], joining [[Devin Harris]], [[Alando Tucker]] and Josh Gasser. He earned Big Ten All-Freshman team recognition as well as honorable mention [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] honors. He was also two-time Big Ten Freshman of the Week (January 14 and March 4, 2013). Dekker scored a season-high 19 points against [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]] on November 24, 2012, and [[Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball|Nebraska]] on February 26, 2013. ===Sophomore season=== Before the season, Dekker was named to the [[Wooden Award]] and [[Naismith College Player of the Year|Naismith Trophy]] watch lists.{{cite web|url=http://www.uwbadgers.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/112113aaa.html|title=Dekker named to Naismith Trophy Watch List|publisher=UWBadgers.com|date=November 21, 2013|access-date=November 21, 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131130020745/http://www.uwbadgers.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/112113aaa.html|archive-date=November 30, 2013}} At the conclusion of the regular season in which he started all 38 games, Dekker was named to the Second Team All-Big Ten by the coaches and Third Team All-Big Ten by the media.{{cite web |url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/031014aag.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140311020018/http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/031014aag.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 11, 2014 |title=Big Ten Announces 2014 Men's Basketball Postseason Honors: Michigan's Stauskas named Big Ten Player of the Year |access-date=March 10, 2014 |date=March 10, 2014 |publisher=[[CBS Interactive]] |work=BigTen.org}} ===Junior season=== Before the season, Dekker was named to the Wooden Award and Naismith Trophy watch lists. At the conclusion of the regular season, Dekker was named to the Second Team All-Big Ten by the coaches and by the media. But he really only took off in the NCAA Tournament. In the Sweet 16 against the number four seeded North Carolina Tar Heels, Dekker scored a career high 23 points and grabbed 10 rebounds to lead the 1-seed Wisconsin to a 79–72 victory. In the Elite 8 against the number 2-seeded Arizona Wildcats, Dekker again came up big, scoring a new career high 27 points, including 5 of the Badgers's 10 second-half threes, the final of which is now known nationally as the "Dekker Dagger" shot because it sealed the win for Wisconsin. For these efforts, he was named West Regional Most Outstanding Player during the [[2015 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament]]. In the Final Four game against the heavily favored and undefeated Kentucky Wildcats, Dekker came through with another huge game, scoring 16 points, including the three that gave Wisconsin the lead for good. The Badgers finished second in the NCAA tournament after losing to Duke in the championship game.{{cite web|url=http://www.csnchicago.com/big-ten/night-sam-dekker-blames-himself-badgers-defeat|title=On off night, Sam Dekker blames himself for Badgers' defeat|publisher=csnchicago.com|author=Vinnie Clippers Acquire Seven Players and Draft Pick, Including Beverley, Dekker, Harrell and Williams|work=NBA.com|date=June 28, 2017|access-date=June 28, 2017}} ===Cleveland Cavaliers (2018)=== On August 7, 2018, Dekker was traded, along with the draft rights to [[Renaldas Seibutis]] and cash considerations, to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in exchange for the draft rights to [[Vladimir Veremeenko]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/dekker-trade-180807|title=Cavaliers Acquire Sam Dekker|work=NBA.com|date=August 7, 2018|access-date=August 7, 2018}} ===Washington Wizards (2018–2019)=== On December 7, 2018, Dekker was traded to the [[Washington Wizards]] in a five-player, three-team deal. The Bucks sent [[John Henson (basketball)|John Henson]], [[Matthew Dellavedova]], and 2021 first- and second-round picks to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] and received [[George Hill (basketball)|George Hill]] and a 2021 second-round pick. The Wizards also sent a 2022 second-round pick to the Cavs.{{cite news|title=Wizards acquire Sam Dekker in three-team |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/europecup/21-22/news/vote-who-do-you-think-will-be-the-fiba-europe-cup-final-mvp |access-date=2022-04-27 |website=FIBA.basketball |language=en}}{{Cite web Finals|Finals]]. === London Lions (2022–2024) === On August 7, 2022, Dekker signed with the [[London Lions (basketball)|London Lions]] of the [[British Basketball League]] (BBL) and the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]].{{Cite web |date=2022-08-07 |title=London Lions sign Sam Dekker |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/eurocup/1375722/london-lions-sign-sam-dekker/ |access-date=2022-08-07 |website=Eurohoops |language=en}} In his inaugural season, the Lions won both the 2022–23 BBL Cup and Championship, and Dekker was the top scorer in the EuroCup regular season. In May, Dekker was named the MVP of the 2022–23 BBL season.{{Cite web |last=Gains |first=Bradley |date=2023-05-12 |title=Sam Dekker scoops BBL MVP award for 2022-23 season |url=https://www.hoopsfix.com/2023/05/sam-dekker-scoops-bbl-mvp-award-for-2022-23-season/ |access-date=2024-02-23 |website=Hoopsfix.com |language=en-US}} In the [[2022–23 EuroCup Basketball|2022-23 Eurocup]] season, club debut in the second european competition, they reached the play-offs but being knocked in the eightfinals against Joventut Badalona. Sam was the best player of the team in the whole season and play-offs, and got into the [[All-Eurocup Second Team|All-Eurocup second team]]. He won the BBL again in the 2023–24 season, becoming MVP of the Final. In the [[2023–24 EuroCup Basketball|2023–24 Eurocup season]] they reached the semi-finals for the first time in the history of the club but also for an english club in European competitions, being knocked by the future champions of the competition, [[Paris Basketball]]. === Joventut Badalona (2024–2026) === On November 12, 2024, Dekker signed a temporary contract with [[Joventut Badalona]], a historic team from Catalonia (Spain) in the [[Liga ACB|ACB]] League.{{Cite web |date=2024-11-12 |title=Sam Dekker refuerza el juego interior de la Penya |url=https://www.acb.com/articulo/ver/484183-sam-dekker-refuerza-el-juego-interior-de-la-penya.html |access-date=2026-02-03 |website=acb.com |language=es}} Joventut was also taking part the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]] but didn't reach the play-offs due to a bad start in the regular season. After achieving qualification in 5th position for the [[Spanish King's Cup (basketball)|Spanish King's Cup]] and his big impact on the team, Sam extended his contract until the end of the season as he became a key player since his arrival.{{Cite web |date=2025-01-14 |title=Sam Dekker, renovado hasta final de temporada |url=https://www.acb.com/articulo/ver/491902-sam-dekker-renovado-hasta-final-de-temporada.html |access-date=2026-02-03 |website=acb.com |language=es}} He was named '''ACB''' ''Week 12 MVP'' after a memorable performance with 30 points (8 three-pointers) and 8 rebounds against [[Básquet_Coruña|Leyma Coruña]].{{Cite web |date=2024-12-22 |title=Sam Dekker, Jugador de la Jornada 12 de la Liga Endesa 2024-25 |url=https://www.acb.com/articulo/ver/489801-sam-dekker-jugador-de-la-jornada-12-de-la-liga-endesa-202425.html |access-date=2026-02-03 |website=acb.com |language=es}} With Joventut finishing in 6th position in the ACB, Dekker averaged 13 points and 4 rebounds per game (41% 3PT). Joventut qualified for the play-offs, falling in the quarterfinals. On August 1, 2025, Sam extended his contract with Joventut Badalona for one more year, until June 2026.{{Cite web |date=2025-08-01 |title=¡Sam Dekker tiene ganas de Penya! |url=https://www.acb.com/articulo/ver/520292-sam-dekker-tiene-ganas-de-penya.html |access-date=2026-02-03 |website=acb.com |language=es}} In February 2026, Dekker reached an agreement to terminate his contract with Joventut in order to travel to the US to seek treatment for recurring shoulder injuries.{{Cite web |date=2026-02-01 |title=Sam Dekker y Joventut Badalona separan sus caminos |url=https://www.acb.com/articulo/ver/547379-joventut-y-sam-dekker-separan-sus-caminos.html |access-date=2026-02-03 |website=acb.com |language=es}} ==Coaching career== On May 15, 2026, Dekker was hired by the [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|University of South Carolina men's basketball team]] as an assistant coach. Dekker played three seasons with Gamecocks head coach [[Lamont Paris]] from 2012-15 while Paris was an assistant at Wisconsin.{{cite web |last1=Whittle |first1=John |title=Sam Dekker added as an assistant basketball coach |url=https://247sports.com/article/sam-dekker-south-carolina-gamecocks-basketball-assistant-coach-285417906/ |website=247Sports |access-date=May 15, 2026}} ==Personal life== Dekker has remained a Sheboygan resident throughout his NBA career.
